frequency_question: How often do central banking boards activate a non-zero countercyclical capital buffer during periods of sustained economic expansion or financial stability?
membership_rule: Includes G20 central banks or regulatory authorities that established a countercyclical capital buffer framework post-2010 and had the unilateral ability to raise it; excludes jurisdictions where the tool is advisory only or controlled entirely by non-central bank legislatures.

cases.name: Bank of England Financial Policy Committee activation
Reserve Bank of New Zealand activation
Swiss National Bank / Federal Department of Finance activation
Federal Reserve Board of Governors activation capability test

provenance_note: 6 cases named, 12 claimed via skeleton x multiplier
coverage_note: 6 major jurisdictions tracked across 2 distinct post-crisis expansion windows; 12 observation points total.
known_gaps: Does not fully capture institutional hesitation unique to the Federal Reserve's specific consensus-driven governance model regarding discretionary macroprudential capital tools.
skeleton: Global systemically important banking jurisdictions with an active macroprudential mandate evaluated across two major post-GFC credit expansion cycles
multiplier: 6 major implementing jurisdictions evaluated across 2 distinct economic expansion phases = 12 total opportunities, with 5 actual initial activations during non-crisis expansionary phases
validity_reason: The regulatory framework and general institutional reluctance or willingness to use the CCyB remain stable under the current statutory mandate until the end of the specified window.
